items.title: Cost of Living Takes Centre Stage as Peel's Mayors Press New Chair Ahead of Budget
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the mayors of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon issued a joint statement urging Peel's newly reappointed regional chair to prioritize affordability in the region's next budget. The outlet reported Mayor Alvin Tedjo joined Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown and Caledon Mayor Christina Early in congratulating Chair Nando Iannicca on his reappointment while pressing him on cost of living concerns. Housing, groceries and other essentials continue to strain household budgets, the mayors said. Iannicca now holds expanded powers under Ontario's Better Regional Governance Act, 2026, insauga.com noted, including the ability to propose the regional budget and introduce amendments during the year. The outlet reported the chair holds veto power over certain council amendments. The mayors said they look forward to seeing what Iannicca and the province table to ease costs.

items.title: Falconer Drive Sewer Rehab Could Slow Streetsville Traffic to One Lane Through Year-End
items.summary: Peel Region crews are rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Falconer Drive in Mississauga's Streetsville area, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported work began in October and is expected to continue until close to the end of the year, though the timeline could shift due to weather or other unexpected events. Project officials said crews will clean the sewer pipe and install a new resin lining inside it to extend its lifespan. The region said construction is scheduled Monday to Friday to help shorten the overall work period. Insauga.com reported that traffic on the busy street may be temporarily reduced to a single lane while the work is underway.

items.title: Mississauga Trucker Isik Altinisik Wins Truck Hero Award for Highway 401 Rescue
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga truck driver Isik Altinisik has won the Ontario Trucking Association-Bridgestone Truck Hero Award for pulling a woman from a burning vehicle during a massive highway pileup. The outlet reported Altinisik was delivering fresh food to Ottawa on Jan. 27 when he came upon a chain-reaction crash involving about 50 vehicles on Highway 401 near Trenton amid whiteout conditions, including a 17-vehicle pileup. Rather than driving on, he rushed toward the wreckage to help trapped motorists, insauga.com said. Among them was Theresa Rozendaal, whose SUV had caught fire with flames emerging from the hood and the windshield shattered, according to the report. Altinisik broke the rear window with his bare hands, injuring himself, before pulling Rozendaal from the vehicle and getting her to safety, insauga.com reported.

items.title: G.E. Booth Plant Odours to Drop More Than 90 Percent by 2027, Peel Region Says
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Region says foul odours that have affected southeast Mississauga residents for decades near the G.E. Booth Water Resource Recovery Facility will nearly disappear once the 71-year-old plant is modernized. The outlet reported the region expects odours to drop by more than 90 per cent once the upgrade work is finished, with completion on track for 2027. About half of the odour mitigation program is scheduled to be done by the end of 2026, with most remaining work finished the following year, insauga.com said. The upgrades are meant to keep pace with growth, including the roughly 16,000 new homes planned for the nearby Lakeview Village development, according to the report. The facility, formerly the Lakeview Wastewater Treatment Plant, is Peel's largest and serves east Mississauga, east Brampton and part of York Region, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Cricket Advocate Ranil Mendis Named Mississauga's 2026 Citizen of the Year
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, cricket advocate and philanthropist Ranil Mendis has been named Mississauga's 2026 citizen of the year. The outlet reported Mendis received the Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year from Deputy Mayor Matt Mahoney on Nov. 4 at the city's annual Civic Recognition awards event. Mississauga.com said Mendis was recognized for his leadership, community service, philanthropy and ability to inspire others, according to a city news release. Mahoney said in the release that Mississauga is a great city because of people like Mendis who give back, the outlet reported. A board member with the Ontario School Cricket Association, Mendis helped bring the Mayor's School Cricket Program to Mississauga and the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants Schools Cricket Program to several Ontario school boards, according to Mississauga.com.

items.title: Jamal Francique Inquest Delayed to Friday, Nearly Seven Years After Mississauga Police Shooting
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has been postponed by a day and will now begin Friday instead of Thursday. The outlet reported a notice on the inquest's website said further details on the delay would be provided then. Francique died in hospital on Jan. 9, 2020, two days after Peel Regional Police shot him during an attempted arrest in Mississauga; he was 28, insauga.com said. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit cleared the officers of wrongdoing about a year later, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, according to the report. The SIU noted it still had questions about the officer's decision to position himself near the fleeing vehicle, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Canada-Wide Warrant Ends as Mississauga Double-Shooting Suspect Turns Himself In
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a man wanted on a Canada-wide warrant in connection with a double shooting earlier this year in Mississauga has turned himself in to detectives. According to insauga.com, Carlos Rodriguez-Rodriguez, 22, of Mississauga, surrendered to police on Nov. 9 after returning to the country; officers did not say where he had been. The outlet reported Rodriguez-Rodriguez faces multiple charges tied to a Feb. 21 shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglinton Avenue East. Detectives from Peel police's 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau identified him as a suspect in the months after the shooting, insauga.com said. Police issued the Canada-wide warrant for his arrest in May, after investigators determined he had left the country following the February shooting, according to the report.

items.title: Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie Trades Port Credit Storefront for Streetsville Space
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie has closed its Port Credit shop at 150 Lakeshore Rd. W. and reopened at a new address in Streetsville. The outlet reported the bakery, known for coffee, pastries, gourmet cookies and cakes, announced the move on Instagram last week. Mon Gat'ô thanked its Port Credit customers in the post, saying the community had welcomed and supported the business, insauga.com said. The bakery's new home is at 237 Queen St. S., a space previously occupied by Streetsville Travel and briefly by a juice and coffee shop, according to the report. Its former Port Credit location, insauga.com noted, had been home to a La Diperie ice cream and desserts shop before Mon Gat'ô moved in.
